channel.title: Frame Foundry blog
channel.description: Gaming PCs, parts, prices, upgrades and games - from a custom PC builder in Los Angeles.

item.title: October price notes: what moved in our parts price log
item.description: Three weeks of daily price checks on the 17 parts in our builds: graphics cards up the most, memory and SSDs up a little, and what it did to build prices.

item.title: Five settings to check on a new gaming PC
item.description: Memory profile, monitor refresh rate, graphics driver, Windows power mode and updates - what each does, where to find it, and which we set before delivery.

item.title: Gaming PC for streaming: what changes, and what does not
item.description: Streaming from a gaming PC needs 32GB of memory, a graphics card with a hardware encoder and enough upload speed. Which of our builds already have all three.

item.title: What "X3D" means on a Ryzen chip, and when it is worth paying for
item.description: AMD's X3D chips carry three times the cache of a regular Ryzen. What that does for games, which of our builds use one, and when $190 is better spent elsewhere.

item.title: 1080p, 1440p or 4K: which monitor fits which build
item.description: How to match a monitor's resolution to a gaming PC - what 1080p, 1440p and 4K ask of the graphics card, which of our builds fits each, and what to buy first.

item.title: Why your gaming PC gets loud and hot after a year or two
item.description: A PC that got loud and slow usually needs a clean, not a new part - dust, dried thermal paste and fan curves explained, with what a $79 tune-up fixes.

item.title: Is my PC worth upgrading, or should I buy new?
item.description: A simple checklist for deciding whether to upgrade a gaming PC or replace it - Windows 11, the part that is actually slow, what the rest can take, and the math.

item.title: Is 16GB of RAM enough for gaming in 2026?
item.description: For today's popular games, 16GB is enough. 32GB is worth it if you stream, edit video or keep a lot open while you play. What it costs right now and how to decide.

item.title: Graphics card and memory prices are climbing this fall - what it means if you are buying
item.description: Average graphics card prices rose about 30-50% since July and DDR5 memory keeps rising, while CPUs and power supplies held steady. What we see and how we price around it.
